PMR's official history identifies the five original 1963 Grand Sports, and a dedicated specification source gives the race car's four-speed manual and single dry-plate clutch.

claims.basis: PMR's official history identifies the five original 1963 Grand Sports, and a dedicated specification source gives the race car's four-speed manual and single dry-plate clutch.

The dedicated specification says four-speed manual. A period front-mounted manual four-speed is an H-pattern manual; no sequential or paddle control is documented. Downshift-only action. Modeled only for upshifts. A manual four-speed with a single dry-plate clutch requires the clutch to launch from rest. The exact chassis 003 cockpit image shows a continuous circular three-spoke rim. Applicability is medium because the record represents the five-car Grand Sport project while the photograph is chassis 003. The fully visible wheel face has no integrated screen; the instruments are mounted in the dashboard behind it. No wheel-mounted shift-light strip or lamps are visible on the fully exposed wheel face in the exact chassis 003 photograph. The photographed rim forms a continuous closed circumference rather than an open-top wheel.
